decisions.reason: Report grounds the two-projection distinction in host-input-contract.ts (draft/Occurrence offsets are clipboard-text, chips expanded) and in host-input-facade.ts (insertReference TokenSpan splices/consumes detectText; tail lookahead reads detectText), correctly stating a chip occupies one U+FFFC in detect coordinates and that plain text and separator spaces count equally in both. No invented APIs; an equivalent description of the contract.

Report identifies snapshot.draft.length in add as the miscomputed value and explains: with an empty composer both projections coincide so paste #1 works; after a chip, clipboard length (29) overshoots the 2-char detect span, insertReference returns false, and the plugin throws the changed-composer toast. It explicitly rejects the concurrency/race reading by noting the rev CAS passes. Grounded in plugin-client.js, the session capture and the facade.

Report traces remove: occurrence.offset/length (clipboard coordinates) passed unconverted to consumeToken, false return ignored, records.delete runs unconditionally, so the live occurrence stays while the dock's record===undefined branch renders 'unavailable' and the composer chip persists. It explicitly ties both symptoms to the same coordinate mismatch rather than a separate upload failure.

Report derives a concrete toDetectPos rule (subtract Σ(length−1) for occurrences entirely before the position), applies it at both call sites — insertion caret at draft end using all preceding occurrences, and removal mapped offset plus a one-detect-character span replacing occurrence.length — keeps the revision guard with re-read discipline, and retires records only after consumeToken returns true (with error state on false). Exceeds 'merely saying convert offsets'.

Regression plan asserts two successive pastes with both chips present, then removing a chip with another preceding chip (remove A with B surviving) asserting occurrence, dock chip and record removed together while the other chip survives. It adds guard-refusal/records-retained, empty-again and phase-guard variants with concrete executable-style assertions, matching the required sequences.
